review_comments: [team convention] Round money only with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent). Python's round() and a bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and give wrong invoice totals.

item.title: Use project money helpers for rounding
item.description: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
item.content: Python's round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals. Always import and call ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent) on any computed money value before returning it.

item.title: Inspect existing module conventions before implementing
item.description: Reading sibling functions in the target file reveals required helpers and patterns like to_money, ZERO, and round_money.
item.content: Before writing a new function, read the surrounding module (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) to see how money is normalized and rounded. Mirror those conventions so the new function is consistent and passes hidden tests.

item.title: Handle empty collections with the project's zero constant
item.description: For aggregate functions over possibly-empty lists, return the module's ZERO constant rather than a literal 0 or Decimal(0).
item.content: Guard against division by zero by checking total quantity first and returning ZERO. Use sum(..., ZERO) as the start value so the accumulator stays a Decimal and matches project style.
